Since \(x,y,z\ge 0\) and \(x+y+z\le 1\), the region is

\[
\Omega=\{(x,y,z):0\le x\le x+y\le x+y+z\le 1\}.
\]

A natural substitution is the cumulative-sum substitution

\[
u=x,\qquad v=x+y,\qquad w=x+y+z.
\]

Then

\[
x=u,\qquad y=v-u,\qquad z=w-v,
\]

and the Jacobian is

\[
\left|\frac{\partial(x,y,z)}{\partial(u,v,w)}\right|=1.
\]

The new region is simply

\[
0\le u\le v\le w\le 1.
\]

Also,

\[
(x+y+z)^2xyz=w^2u(v-u)(w-v).
\]

Thus

\[
I=\int_0^1\int_0^w\int_0^v w^2u(v-u)(w-v)\,du\,dv\,dw.
\]

Compute the inner integral:

\[
\int_0^v u(v-u)\,du=\frac{v^3}{6}.
\]

So

\[
I=\frac16\int_0^1 w^2\int_0^w v^3(w-v)\,dv\,dw.
\]

Next,

\[
\int_0^w v^3(w-v)\,dv
=
w\frac{w^4}{4}-\frac{w^5}{5}
=
\frac{w^5}{20}.
\]

Hence

\[
I=\frac16\int_0^1 w^2\cdot \frac{w^5}{20}\,dw
=
\frac1{120}\int_0^1 w^7\,dw
=
\frac1{120}\cdot\frac18
=
\frac1{960}.
\]

\[
\boxed{u=x,\;v=x+y,\;w=x+y+z\quad\text{gives}\quad \int_\Omega (x+y+z)^2xyz\,dxdydz=\frac{1}{960}}
\]
